subject.title: openclaw models fallbacks {list,add,remove,clear} ignores --agent, always operates on agents.defaults.model.fallbacks

question: Should `models fallbacks` become a per-agent text-model editor, or should all fallback command groups remain defaults-only and reject inherited `--agent` scope?
rationale: Both directions are internally coherent, but choosing how writes materialize an override for agents currently inheriting defaults changes the public CLI and configuration inheritance contract.

options.title: Honor text agent scope
options.body: Add agent-aware text fallback reads and writes with explicit inheritance rules, while rejecting agent scope for image fallbacks.

options.title: Keep defaults-only commands
options.body: Preserve the documented defaults-only behavior but fail clearly whenever inherited or local `--agent` scope is supplied.

options.title: Add a separate agent editor
options.body: Keep `models fallbacks` defaults-only and expose per-agent model-chain editing through a distinct agents-focused CLI surface.

recommendation.title: Honor text agent scope
recommendation.body: Add agent-aware text fallback reads and writes with explicit inheritance rules, while rejecting agent scope for image fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns the established public models CLI contract and its agent-aware status behavior.
